---
title: "Indicators: limitations"
---

## Summary

The indicators describe what the registrar records, nothing more. Companies House treats its
register as unverified information supplied by companies, identity checks are only part-way
rolled out, and absence of a flag is weak evidence rather than a clean bill of health. The
validation is positive-unlabelled, so it measures conditional recall, not accuracy against
negative ground truth; and detecting insolvency is a narrow proxy, not a measure of
trustworthiness, fraud or creditworthiness. Read the flags as traceable evidence to weigh, never
as a verdict or a score.

## Details

- Companies House describes its register as unverified information supplied by companies.
  ECCTA identity verification is rolling out and does not retrospectively verify all officer
  or PSC identities.
- Officer/PSC same-person joins are fuzzy when based on names and partial dates of birth.
  Personal data remains local and is not published by this project.
- Validation is positive-unlabelled: it measures conditional recall, not precision. The
  assumed-negative control has no negative ground truth.
- Insolvency is an adjacent proxy for the broader and subjective idea of trustworthiness.
  Detecting insolvency does not validate trustworthiness, fraud, creditworthiness, or future
  solvency.
- API current state, monthly snapshot state, and Insolvency Service labels from the 2012–2024
  window are three distinct time bases. Apparent disagreement can reflect timing rather than
  a pipeline error.
- Absence of a flag is weak evidence. Rules cover defined recorded facts and do not form a
  composite score or comprehensive due-diligence conclusion.
